==English==
{{wp}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|bo͝ok}}, {{IPA|en|/bʊk/}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-book.ogg|a=UK}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-book.ogg|a=US}}
* {{enPR|bo͞ok}} {{IPA|en|/buːk/|aa=some speakers from <<Northern England>> and <<Ireland>>}}
* {{IPA|en|/bʉk/|a=Scotland,NI,MLE}}
* {{homophones|en|buck|aa=<<non-foot-strut split>>, when pronounced /bʊk/}}
* {{rhymes|en|ʊk|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=Q571|:inh|enm:bok<id:book>|tree=1}}
[[File:Pieni2.jpg|right|thumb|A hard-cover '''book''' ({{senseno|en|Q571}})]]
From {{inh|en|enm|bok}}, {{m|enm|book}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bōc}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*bōk}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*bōks}}. ''Bookmaker'' sense by {{clipping|en|nocap=1}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|beuk}}, {{m|sco|buik}}, {{m|sco|buke|t=book}}, {{cog|yol|buke|t=book}}, {{cog|frr|Bok}}, {{m|frr|buk}}, {{m|frr|bök|t=book}}, {{cog|stq|Bouk|t=book}}, {{cog|fy|-}}, {{cog|nl|boek|t=book}}, {{cog|gsw|Buech|t=book}}, {{cog|bar|Buach|t=book}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|Booch}}, {{m|gmw-cfr|Buch|t=book}}, {{cog|de|-}}, {{cog|lb|Buch|t=book}}, {{cog|nds-de|Book|t=book}}, {{cog|li|book}}, {{m|li|Bouk|t=book}}, {{cog|wym|büch|t=book}}, {{cog|yi|בוך|t=book}}, {{cog|da|bog|t=book}}, {{cog|ovd|buok|t=book}}, {{cog|fo|-}}, {{cog|is|bók|t=book}}, {{cog|nb|-}}, {{cog|nn|-}} and {{cog|sv|bok|t=book}}. 
{{col-bottom}}

====Alternative forms====
* {{alt|en|boke||obsolete}}
* {{alt|en|booke||archaic}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{sid|en|Q571}} A collection of sheets of paper bound together to hinge at one edge, containing printed or written material, pictures, etc.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|act=I|scene=ii|page=3|column=1|passage=Knowing I lou'd my '''bookes''', he furniſhd me / From mine owne Library, with volumes, that / I prize aboue my Dukedome.}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1962|translator=James East Irby|author=w:Luis Borges|title=w:The Library of Babel
|passage=I repeat: it suffices that a '''book''' be possible for it to exist. Only the impossible is excluded. For example: no '''book''' can be a ladder, although no doubt there are '''books''' which discuss and negate and demonstrate this possibility and others whose structure corresponds to that of a ladder.}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1983|author=Steve Horelick; et al|title=w:Reading Rainbow
|passage=I can be anything.<br>Take a look!<br>It's in a '''book''':<br>A reading rainbow.}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1991|author=w:Stephen Fry|title=[[:w:The Liar (novel)|The Liar]]|page=51
|passage=Trefusis's quarters could be described in one word. '''Books'''. '''Books''' and '''books''' and '''books'''. And then, just when an observer might be lured into thinking that that must be it, more '''books'''... Trefusis himself was highly dismissive of them. ‘Waste of trees,’ he had once said. ‘Stupid, ugly, clumsy, heavy things. The sooner technology comes up with a reliable alternative the better... The world is so fond of saying that '''books''' should be “treated with respect”. But when are we told that ''words'' should be treated with respect?’}}
#: {{ux|en|She opened the '''book''' to page 37 and began to read aloud.}}
#: {{ux|en|He was frustrated because he couldn't find anything about dinosaurs in the '''book'''.}}
# A long work fit for [[publication]], typically [[prose]], such as a [[novel]] or [[textbook]], and typically published as such a bound collection of sheets, but now sometimes electronically as an [[e-book]].
#: {{ux|en|I have three copies of his first '''book'''.}}
#* {{quote-web|en|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/archive/2022/12/chatgpt-ai-writing-college-student-essays/672371/|title=The College Essay Is Dead|date=2022-12-06|author=w:Stephen Marche|quotee=w:Sam Bankman-Fried|work=The Atlantic|passage= “I would never read a '''book''',” he once told an interviewer. “I don’t want to say no '''book''' is ever worth reading, but I actually do believe something pretty close to that.”}}
#* {{RQ:Pacifik Wonderfool|Freethinker|passage=They read some '''books'''<br>Sharing their moods<br>They know everything<br>Whatever it can mean}}
# A major division of a long work.
#: {{syn|en|tome|volume}}
#: {{ux|en|Genesis is the first '''book''' of the Bible.}}
#: {{ux|en|Many readers find the first '''book''' of ''A Tale of Two Cities'' to be confusing.}}
# {{senseid|en|gambling}} {{lb|en|gambling}} A record of betting (from the use of a notebook to record what each person has bet).
#: {{ux|en|I'm running a '''book''' on who is going to win the race.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} A [[bookmaker]] (a person who takes bets on sporting events and similar); [[bookie]]; [[turf accountant]].
# A convenient collection, in a form resembling a book, of small paper items for individual use.
#: {{syn|en|booklet}}
#: {{co|en|a '''book''' of stamps}}
#: {{co|en|a '''book''' of raffle tickets}}
#: {{co|en|a '''book''' of matches ([[matchbook]])}}
# {{lb|en|theatre}} The script of a [[musical]] or [[opera]].
#: {{syn|en|libretto}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=2010|author=David Baskerville; Tim Baskerville|title=Music Business Handbook and Career Guide|page=172
|passage=The guild helps ensure that the ownership and control of the music, lyrics, and '''book''' of a show remain in the hands of its authors and composers—not the producers.}}
# {{lb|en|usually|in the plural}} Records of the accounts of a business.
#: {{syn|en|account|record}}
# {{lb|en|legal|colloquial}} A [[book award]], a recognition for receiving the highest grade in a class (traditionally an actual book, but recently more likely a letter or certificate acknowledging the achievement).
# {{lb|en|whist}} Six [[trick]]s taken by one side.
# {{lb|en|poker slang}} [[four of a kind|Four of a kind]].<ref>Weisenberg, Michael (2000) ''[http://www.poker1.com/mcu/pokerdictionary/mculib_dictionary_info.asp The Official Dictionary of Poker].'' MGI/Mike Caro University. {{ISBN|978-1880069523}}</ref>
# {{lb|en|sports}} A document, held by the referee, of the incidents that happened in a game.
# {{lb|en|sports|by extension}} A list of all players who have been booked (received a warning) in a game.
#* {{quote-web|en|date=March 2, 2011
|author=Andy Campbell
|title=Celtic 1 - 0 Rangers
|work=BBC
|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/9409758.stm
|page=
|passage=Celtic captain Scott Brown joined team-mate Majstorovic in the '''book''' and Rangers' John Fleck was also shown a yellow card as an ill-tempered half drew to a close.}}
# {{lb|en|horse racing}} The list of [[mare]]s that a [[stallion]] will [[breed]] in a given season.
# {{lb|en|horse racing}} A list of the [[race]]s that a [[jockey]] is scheduled to ride in.
# {{lb|en|cartomancy}} The twenty-sixth [[Lenormand]] card.
# {{lb|en|figurative}} Any source of instruction.
# {{lb|en|with "the"}} The accumulated body of knowledge passed down among [[black]] [[pimp]]s.
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1974|author=Adrienne Lanier Seward|title=The Black Pimp as a Folk Hero|page=11
|passage='''The Book''' is an oral tradition of belief in The Life that has been passed down from player to player from generation to generation.}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1994|title=Antiquarian Book Monthly|volume=21|page=36
|passage=On the other hand '''The Book''' is an oral tradition containing the rules and principles to be adopted by a pimp who wishes to be a player.}}
# {{lb|en|advertising|informal}} A [[portfolio]] of one's previous work in the industry.
#* {{quote-text|en|year=2017|author=Nik Mahon|title=Basics Advertising 02: Art Direction|page=8
|passage=Getting your '''book''' (portfolio) organised is the first step, and knowing both what to include, and what to leave out, is an essential step towards achieving that important agency placement.}}
#* ''Idea Industry'' (page 27)
#*: Your portfolio — your '''book''' — has to be killer.
# {{lb|en|chess|uncountable}} The [[sum]] of [[chess]] [[knowledge]] in the [[opening]] or [[endgame]].
#: {{ux|en|The {{w|Opposite-colored bishops endgame|opposite-colored bishops endgame}} is usually a '''book''' draw.}}
#: {{co|en|A [[book move|'''book''' move]]}}
#: {{co|en|[[out of book|out of '''book''']]}}
#* {{quote-web|en|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230112080030/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/apr/06/schoolboy-vincent-keymer-wins-grenke-open|work=w:The Guardian|passage=White to move and win. How can he do it? The BK plans a march to h8, eating the f4 pawn en route, for a '''book''' draw.|title=Chess: Schoolboy Vincent Keymer secures shock triumph at Grenke Open|date=2018-04-06|author=w:Leonard Barden}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=How to Swindle in Chess|passage=This seems certain to simplify into a battle between White's king, rook and two pawns against Black's king and rook. In some cases a '''book''' draw is possible. But a '''book''' win is more likely.|year=2020|author=w:Andrew Soltis|isbn=9781849945639|publisher=w:Batsford Books}}
# {{lb|en|historical}} A [[package]] of [[silk]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1867|author=John I. Knight|journal=Mechanics Magazine|page=52
|passage=This machinery was provided with a rotary drum with received upon its periphery the "'''books'''" of silk to be operated upon and presented them to travelling, combing, or dressing surfaces. The '''books''' were clamped and released automatically by the aid of bars formed with wedges and put in operation by screws {{...}}}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|booken}}, {{m|enm|boken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bōcian}}, {{m|ang|ġebōcian}}, from the noun (see above).

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{senseid|en|reserve}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[reserve]] (something) for future use.
#: {{syn|en|reserve}}
#: {{ux|en|I want to '''book''' a hotel room for tomorrow night.}}
#: {{ux|en|I can '''book''' tickets for the concert next week.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2020 December 2|author=Paul Bigland|title=My weirdest and wackiest Rover yet|journal=Rail|page=68|text=I haven't '''booked''', so I don't have a clue as to whether the service will be busy or not. Supposedly, reservations are compulsory, but I want to find out what would happen if you just turn up.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[write down]], to [[register]] or [[record]] in a book or as in a book.
#: {{syn|en|[[make]] a [[note]] of|[[note]] [[down]]|record|write down}}
#: {{ux|en|They '''booked''' that message from the hill.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To add a [[name]] to the [[list]] of people who are [[participating]] in something.
#: {{syn|en|sign up|register|reserve|schedule|enroll}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''booked''' a flight to New York.}}
# {{lb|en|law enforcement|transitive}} To [[record]] the name and other details of a suspected offender and the offence for later judicial action.
#: {{ux|en|The police '''booked''' him for driving too fast.}}
# {{lb|en|sports}} To issue a [[caution]] to, usually a [[yellow card]], or a [[red card]] if a yellow card has already been issued.
# {{lb|en|intransitive|slang}} To travel very fast.
#: {{syn|en|bomb|hurtle|rocket|speed|shoot|whiz}}
#: {{ux|en|He was really '''booking''' until he passed the speed trap.}}
# To record [[bet|bets]] as [[bookmaker]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|law student slang}} To receive the highest [[grade]] in a class.
#: {{ux|en|The top three students had a bet on which one was going to '''book''' their intellectual property class.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|slang}} To [[move]] or [[leave]], often hurriedly and abruptly.
#: {{ux|en|He was here earlier, but he '''booked'''.}}

===Etymology 3===
From {{inh|en|enm|book}}, {{m|enm|bok}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bōc}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*bōk}}, first and third person singular indicative past tense of {{der|en|gem-pro|*bakaną|t=to bake}}.
